models.name: Apple tree

models.ask: a small orchard apple tree, a short twisty trunk, a spreading rounded crown with clusters of red apples

scores.label: Outline match
scores.help: Share of the concept silhouette and the model silhouette that coincide

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.824: the umbrella dome, the S-curved trunk and the hanging apple cluster on the right all line up.
The red apples read clearly against the two greens at small size; the crown edge is jagged with leaf tips, not a smooth ball.
Under budget at 2,980 triangles, mostly spent on the crown silhouette (tufts and leaf cards) and the apples.
off: The sheet's three trees are taller and narrower (height/width 1.2 to 1.33) than the hero's crown (about 1.09) and each leans its own way, so they are not views of one tree. Per the AD the hero wins, which caps the sheet views at about 0.66 to 0.74.
The hero's crown is hundreds of small individual leaves; mine is faceted tufts with 330 leaf cards, so the flat facets of the tufts still show between leaves close up.
The hero's trunk is a thick, gnarled, partly split S with a knot; mine is a single lobed twisting tube with a softer S.
The hero has about 80 apples; I kept to the AD's 30 to 50 (46 plus 6 hanging) to stay in budget.
The hero camera yaw is not identifiable for a round tree, so the trunk was laid out for yaw 0 (the orientation that scored best on the sheet), and the hero number is a guide.
steps: First build: S-trunk from hero measurements, 20 smooth subdiv-2 blobs on a measured dome outline, 150 leaf cards, 40 apples, grass pad. Apples were buried in the blobs; 3,508 tris.
Blobs swapped for 36 faceted icosahedron tufts sitting inside the outline, 320 leaf cards, apples moved onto the surface, crown underside raised, trunk clamped at z 0. 3,028 tris.
Bigger apples (0.13 to 0.16 m radius, 48), inner core blob raised out of the trunk gap, darker greens, hanging apples moved to the hero's right.
Hanging cluster lower and further in (6 apples).
Stronger trunk lobes, limbs lowered so they show under the crown, 330 bigger leaf cards laid more along the surface.
Stronger S in the lower trunk; orientation scan over 8 yaws (0.664 to 0.702 mean), picked yaw 0.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and score; to_game.py apple-tree.
details: Short brown stems on the hanging apples, a ragged grass pad with a few blades at the trunk foot, and the limbs peeking out under the crown rim.

Stones are plain jittered blocks, not rounded cobbles.

Heavier ridge beam kicked up at both ends with a 0.55 m front overhang, shorter tie-beam ends, more back overhang, leaf swung closer to the wall, wider footing, stepping stones.

Front braces shortened clear of the door jambs, lighter recess planks, thicker tool handles, deeper hayloft ledge; a sweep of gable overhang, ridge kick, footing and pitch found no further gain.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and score.
details: A strut under the ridge-beam overhang, stepping stones at the doorway, a stump beside the bench, a latch on the leaf, and a squaring diagonal in the planned stage's string lines.

Stretcher and end rails lowered to 0.17 m and thickened (0.10 m), legs lean 3 cm outward along X, braces from x 0.50 to 0.24; lowering the stretcher further to 0.155 m scored lower and was reverted. Final 768 px / 48 samples render.

scores.label: Outline match
scores.help: Share of the concept silhouette and the model silhouette that coincide

good: It reads as an airy weeping birch: fine threads of loose leaf cards with sky between them, the white trunk with black patches visible up through the crown, and arching branch tops above the leaves.

3.8k triangles, under the 4k budget.

The sheet's front and side views are different lopsided trees, as noted before.

The dark base reads as a smooth brown sleeve rather than rough bark.
steps: First build: S-curved trunk, bark patches, 11 arching branches, wide (0.42 m) smooth V-section ribbons hanging to 2.0 to 2.7 m. Read as a banana plant. Targets re-keyed in views/ to get the white trunk back and drop the ground line. Hero scored at a 45/12 guess.
Ribbons replaced by chains of twisted sawtooth leaf cards; narrower crown (radius 1.65), curtains end higher (2.6 to 3.4 m). Hero camera calibrated to 30/10.
Wider, lower crown for the hero (radius 1.8, tips 2.3 to 3.0 m, long strands on the +X side to 1.5 to 2.0 m), cheaper 3-sided branches.
Crown top leans -X as in the hero; fewer card rows and inner curtains to get under 3k. The gaps that opened cost IoU.
Fuller cards (0.5 m, neck 0.5, twist 15 deg), crown radius x0.85, 12 branches x 4 curtains.
Narrower crown top, a 20 deg window in the curtains so the trunk shows, Leaf_Light toned down.
13 branches, using the triangles freed in round 6.
Bark: bigger black diamonds below 2 m, thin bands above, taller ragged dark base (0.75 m).
Half the outer curtains Leaf_Dark (was a third), Leaf_Light slightly duller, for the hero's mix of greens.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and score; to_game.py birch.

AD round: curtains rebuilt as about 80 thinner threads of loose, randomised diamond leaf cards (size, spacing, turn, tilt), one green per thread with 20% of cards in the other, dark threads inside, threads fanned per branch so the crown is open, branch crests above the leaves, broader crown top, budget 4k. Final 768/48.
details: The ragged dark base sleeve, and leaf cards that shrink towards each thread's tip.

scores.label: Outline match
scores.help: Share of the concept silhouette and the model silhouette that coincide

good: Front 0.837 and back 0.843 against the re-keyed sheet views: head, ear span, horn spacing and the plump pear body agree well.
Hero silhouette 0.79 from the hero's own direction; the render reads as the same toy: big head, huge pink muzzle, rosy cheeks, smile, brass bell under the chin, round patches.
Still clearly a cow and a working game piece: the three poses are rotations of the same parts and the bell hangs plumb in each.
off: The sheet's side view is three-quarter (0.698, proportion guide only, not in the mean). Its head sits higher and further back over the chest and its legs are shorter than the hero's; the hero won.

Hero: the MJ ears are bigger and stick out more horizontally, and the rump reaches a little further back; enlarging the ears, widening the horn spacing or lengthening the rump each lowered both the hero and sheet scores, so they stayed as they are.

Footprint ratio: 2.4 m long by 1.5 m wide over the ears (body 0.88 m wide), against the normal cow's 2.25 by 0.73. The chibi head and ears can't be made that narrow without losing the design; the game scales by the longest side, so the ranch planner sees the same length.
Faceted low-poly rather than the hero's smooth plush (the game uses flat normals); the hero's subtle hair swirl on the forehead is a plain cream bump.
The sheet's tan forelock and small brow spots are not modelled (the hero shows a cream forelock and no head spots).
steps: First charming build from the normal cow's structure: round skull + huge muzzle, plush barrel, stubby legs, decals, big bell; views re-keyed; camera guessed at yaw -40.
Head group x1.12 and wider, bigger flatter ears, warmer colours, longer body, feeding solver keeps the head in front of the chest (neck pivot moved deep into the chest).
Head x1.28, body 8 cm taller (worse on its own: ears too low and wide, head yawed off centre).
Pear section (narrow shoulders, wide low belly), ears higher and smaller, hero camera calibrated on a grid (yaw -50, 6 up).
Thicker upright horns, cheeks fixed (the decal rays missed), taller dome and forelock, head roll removed (it shifted the whole silhouette sideways).
Tried the head 8 cm back and up and x1.34 with bigger ears: worse on every view, reverted.
Head turned 12 deg toward the viewer's side, camera refined to yaw -52, 8 up.
Nose lifted 8 deg, thicker legs and hooves.

Collar re-tilted so it dips under the chin and the bell shows in front of the chest; bell enlarged 25 %; feeding face limited to 78 deg pitch so it looks down at the grass; a 2 deg head roll kept for the storybook tilt.
Tried bigger ears, wider horns, a longer rump and a sideways tail, then the rump and tail alone: both worse, reverted. Final 768 px / 48 sample render.
details: grazes and rests in the pasture

Rosy cheeks, a little smile, a cream forelock bump, cupped pink-lined ears, an oversized bell with a clapper ball, a tail that kicks out to the side, and a rest pose with the front legs stuck out forward like a sitting plush toy.

The construction stages share one design and grow cleanly from stakes to the finished shed.

The illustration's lower, more frontal camera also shows the ridge log and front roof edge higher and further left than the harness's fixed hero camera can, and its walls look shallower than the sheet's (I compromised at a depth of 0.8 x the width).

Tie-beam ends shortened (they poked through the roof), grain pulled closer to the door.

Five thicker ragged shingle courses, each with 5 notched tabs and dark-teal undersides and edges. Warmer, more saturated gold grain spread around the scoop. good: Hero IoU 0.644 (768 px, 48 samples): fountain clump with an upright centre, arches on both sides and tips falling towards the ground, wider than tall like the hero.

off: The hero's pinnae are long, separate, serrated leaflets; mine are one saw-tooth ribbon per side, so up close the fronds look more like fir sprigs than lacy fern. At tile scale (a few pixels) this is not visible.

The hero's left side has two big high arches reaching the far edge at 75-85 % height; mine fall a little lower and closer in, and the IoU is noisy (+-0.02) with the random seed because each frond's azimuth moves.
Fronds that point at the camera are foreshortened, so the centre of the clump is a little less dense than the hero's solid mass.
The rachis strip is barely visible except on the upright centre fronds.
steps: First build: 15 fronds in 3 rings, narrow blades (half-width 0.15-0.17 of length), shallow saw-tooth. 915 tris.
Blades nearly twice as wide (0.27-0.29), 16 fronds, less sag. Fronds still too low and splayed.
Steeper starts and deeper notches; no gain (arches crested too low).
Per-ring arc power, arcs fitted to the hero's crest/tip positions (rise nearly vertical, fall late).

Tip twist, yellower olive greens matched to the hero, longer skirt.
Bigger dark crown (mound and blades), taller centre fronds.
Crown blades lie nearly flat and reach further, filling the bottom of the silhouette.

details: A short skirt of fronds and flat dark crown blades so the clump sits solidly on the ground, and a slight twist towards each frond tip so drooping tips still show their face.

good: Side and front silhouettes match well (IoU 0.82 each): the long upright neck, the big head carried high, the swept-back horns, the sideways ears, the beard, the upright tail and the slim legs.

scores.label: Outline match
scores.help: Share of the concept silhouette and the model silhouette that coincide

good: The three silhouette pieces read at small size: the block basin, the teal canopy and the pump handle sweeping out to the right.
Light: 2406 triangles for the complete model against a 9k budget; 14 objects, one material each, flat colours.
Material names carry the game roles: Stone_Cream, Stone_Dark, Timber_Brown, Roof_Teal, Water_Clear, Metal_Iron, Plank_Bucket (plus Rope_Twine for the planned string lines).
off: The hero is not structurally consistent: its right post hangs behind the pump and stops in mid air, and its two posts would stand in the water if the ridge ran parallel to the basin. I put the posts on the coping and turned the canopy 14 degrees, so the canopy covers the back-left of the basin like the hero but is not square to it.

The pump stands at the back-right corner as the brief asks; the hero draws it nearer the middle of the back rim, so the handle tip sits a little further right than the hero's (handle shortened to compensate).
The left post stands just inside the left coping and runs down to the ground beside the stone face.
Stones are flat-coloured boxes with no painted cracks or wear; the hero's water ripples and splash spray are reduced to a flat slab and a small splash ring.

The remaining IoU gap is mostly the basin's lower-right corner and the top-left of the coping (the perspective of the render camera against the illustration), and the hero's slightly lower, wider roof.
steps: First build: basin, posts on the back corners, canopy with ridge along X over the back, pump at the back-right corner. Harness hero direction (0.62,-0.78,0.42).

Read the hero's geometry: canopy smaller and steeper (pitch 0.8, 1.5 m ridge), moved over the back-left and turned 28 degrees so both posts land on the coping; pump to the back rim; pump and handle heights from the hero.
Tried the canopy square to the basin (yaw 0) with a longer roof and taller basin: worse (0.641). Swept yaw 0/14/20/26 and settled on 14 degrees with the canopy centre at (-0.25, 0.58).

Measured the hero camera (about 19 degrees elevation) and set the check to that elevation; basin lowered to 0.79 m to the coping top; pump top to 1.33 m; handle reach shortened from 0.85 to 0.62 m so the grip ends just past the basin as in the hero.

Canopy centre to (-0.35, 0.55); posts to the ground; outward knee braces trimmed to stay under the roof; coping no longer hides the timber band; bucket stave teeth removed; pump rebuilt with barrel, collars and upper column; thicker handle; greyer stone.
Final render at 768 px, 48 samples. Hero IoU 0.715 with the measured-elevation check; 0.701 from the harness's own hero camera direction (0.62,-0.78,0.42).
details: Iron bolt heads on the timber band, a vent knob on the spout, a small splash ring where the stream meets the water, and post marker pegs plus a chalk outline in the planned stage.

Built the T-post on a two-layer plank base, the lashed crossbeam with chunky end caps and a raised centre hump, the Y-shaped knee braces, the pointed iron finial, and two shallow pans each on one hanger rope that splits into three cords at a knot.

The beam is its own object pivoting on a bronze pin held between two carved yoke cheeks on the post top. Each hanger (rope, knot, three cords, pan) is a child of the beam with its origin at the tie-on point, and is keyed with the exact opposite angle on the same frames, so the pans stay plumb on every frame.

Bevelled, slightly jittered timbers, a rope collar binding the post foot with a loose rope tail and coil on the base, rope lashings at both hang points and around the beam centre, rolled pan rims with a lighter bronze inside, and a bronze pin head.
All three animated objects share one action, exported with export_anim_scene_split_object=False so the GLB carries a single 120-frame clip instead of one clip per object.

Moved the proportions toward the hero illustration (taller and more open, bigger and deeper pans, a broad, thick plank base with the stone resting on it), added the four-turn rope wrap on the post foot and knotted beam-end lashings as low-poly torus rings, and gave every bevelled edge a darker chamfer material so the wood reads two-tone. Still flat colours, no textures.
details: One 120-frame clip at 24 fps that loops seamlessly (rest pose at frames 1 and 102-120). The beam rocks about its bronze pin (local Y axis at z = 0.98 m): +6.5 degrees at f16, -5.5 at f36, +3.5 at f53, -2.0 at f68, +1.0 at f81, -0.35 at f92, then 0 from f102. hanger_left and hanger_right are children of the beam, pivoting at their tie-on points, and are keyed with the exact negative angle on the same frames and interpolation, so the pans swing up and down on the beam ends but always hang straight down. The iron finial is part of the beam and acts as the pointer needle.
Blender 5.2 (bpy), built from Python by the modeler, directed by the art director

The knee braces double as tilt stops: their pads sit just under the beam, so at full tilt the beam nearly touches them, which explains why the swing is limited. I added a bronze pivot pin through carved yoke cheeks, rope lashings at each hang point, little binding knots on every cord, rolled pan rims with a lighter bronze inner face, a rope collar and loose rope tail with a coil at the post foot (from the hero), and a stack of flat stone weights behind the base for the merchant.

good: Reads as the hero at a glance: tall leaning bell gambrel, cream trim, coral shingles, fat silo with a red dome, crooked cupola with a rooster.
9,656 triangles (under the 10k budget) in 14 named meshes; origin on the ground at the footprint centre, Z up, front -Y, 15.2 m tall to the rooster.
Mean IoU went from 0.644 to 0.708 over five measured rounds.
off: The turnaround views are tall, narrow and inconsistent with each other and with the hero (no annex, a wooden-banded red silo, a sloped fantasy roof in the side view). I scored against them as given but followed the hero, so the annex and the cream silo show as blue (render only) in the front and back overlays, and the flat ridge in the side view does not match the sheet's sloping one.
The hero's shingles are bigger and more hand-cut; mine are tidier and smaller per tab to stay in budget.
No recessed porch between the main barn and the annex, and the hero's barrels, mailbox-like posts and the flower beds along the stone base are simplified to a few bushes.
Planks are only battens on the front gable; side walls are plain.
steps: Main barn is a 4.8 m wide, 7 m long body under a tall bell-curved gambrel (Catmull-Rom profile with flared eaves) rising to a 10.1 m ridge, with a crooked cupola and rooster vane on top; the shape is then sheared so the whole barn leans 1.1 m toward the silo.

Every roof (main, annex, cupola) is covered by procedural courses of rounded hexagonal tabs, staggered every other row, lifted at the butt so they overlap, with random jitter and two shingle colours. They are single-sided plus a thick butt skirt, so each tab is 10 triangles.

Round-top double doors in a cream arch frame, two small arched windows and a tall arched window with flower boxes, an oval loft window, plank battens, cream barge boards and corner posts, and a stone sill.

A lower +X wing with its own curvy gable, round window, round-top doors and a coral ramp; behind it a fat, slightly barrel-shaped cream silo with a teal band, red dome, teal finial and two framed windows.
A teal hay-hoist beam with a scroll end pokes out over the front gable, and a glowing lantern hangs from it.
A wobbly grass island with stepping stones to the big doors and flowering bushes.
details: One 120-frame scene clip at 24 fps, seamless. The main round-top doors (door_left, door_right) swing outward on their hinge edges to 100 degrees with a small overshoot, hold, then swing shut with a little bounce; the annex doors (annex_door_left/right) do the same 8 frames later. The weathervane (rooster plus arrow, parented to the tilted cupola) turns a full 360 degrees in gusty steps with back-swings, and the lantern under the hoist beam sways +-7 degrees.

The whole barn leans as one sheared body while the cupola tilts the other way; a scroll-ended teal hoist beam with a glowing lantern that sways; stepping-stone path to the doors; flower bushes on a wobbly grass island; gusty weathervane motion instead of a constant spin.

off: The side view (0.52) scores lowest, because the turnaround's side tree has a broad umbrella top and sprays facing the viewer, which conflict with the hero; I followed the hero.

steps: The turnaround views include the sheet's tan ground band, which the target mask counted as part of the tree; fix_views.py paints the band back to sky colour (keeping the root pixels) and crops below the root line into models/cedar-upgrade/views/, which is what I scored against. The labels (front, side, back) were fine.

One fluted, tapering trunk mesh (24 sides, 11 flutes that twist slightly with height) that stays thick all the way up (0.3 m radius at the top), leans gently left, and has 7 lobed buttress roots built into the radius function. It uses warm red-brown CedarBark #8A4A35, with a lighter BarkStreak material on 7 flute columns for vertical streaks.

Each spray is a fan of flattened, tapered frond blades (wide at the base, pointed and drooping at the tip, arched over a raised midrib, with backward-pointing serration teeth on both edges), splayed outward like fingers in 4 stacked layers: dark below, then dark, mid and light on top, each layer shorter, narrower and lifted. A few short strands hang under some lower-layer tips. The silhouette edge is jagged and pointy, not straight-cut.

The foliage follows the hero: big sprays alternating left/right up the trunk (low W at 6.2 m, low E 7.9, mid W 10.0, mid E 11.4, plus a smaller back spray for depth), with sky and red trunk between them, and the top 25% a dense, slightly lopsided cluster of 6 frond sprays (one radiating all the way round) that hides the trunk tip.
Seven thin, crooked bare branches (3 kinked segments each, plus forked twigs) stick out of the trunk between the tiers, mostly at mid height, as in the hero, in a greyer DeadWood material.

crown_pivot (an empty at z 8.4) carries the upper trunk, the upper sprays and the upper dead branches, and rocks about 0.9 degrees; every one of the 11 spray clumps nods about 3 degrees about its own limb root on two axes with offset phases (alternating 1 and 2 cycles per loop). Frames 1 to 121 keyed, so the 120-frame loop is seamless; exports as one 'Scene' clip.
details: crown_pivot rocks the upper trunk, the upper sprays and the upper dead branches about 0.9 degrees. Each of the 11 spray_* clumps nods about 3 degrees on its own limb pivot, on two axes, with offset phases (alternating 1 and 2 cycles per loop). steps: The turnaround labels are right (front and side show the door, back shows the swing), but each crop had the sheet's shadow band and a sliver of the neighbouring tree; prep_views.py cleans them into views/ and scoring uses that folder.

A custom swept spline (Catmull-Rom, parallel-transport frames) tapering from 2.55 m to 0.42 m, with five flutes twisting 1.1 turns. It follows the hero's big S: hard right at the base (+2.3 m), back left through the middle (-1.2 m), right again into the crown. The flared base is about 5 m wide and swallows the door; four tapered roots.

Three tiers of cloud pads. Each pad is 6 to 9 overlapping flattened UV-sphere puffs of varied size, smooth shaded: a raised central dome, then a ring of smaller lumps with squashed, rounded undersides that make a bulging lip, so no edge is a vertical wall. The crown is 9.9 m wide and 2.7 m deep (3.6:1). Up-facing faces get LeafLight.
Each pad sits on its own tapered swept arm from the trunk, with two forked twigs reaching into the pad.
The low branch reaches 5.6 m out to the left with its own small plate. The two knotted ropes and the bevelled seat hang 3.7 m from it, well clear of the trunk.
Arched red plank door with iron hinges and knob in a dark recess between two roots at the front (-Y), a grass disc, bushes, rocks and a stepping-stone path to the door.
Art-director palette, stored exactly in the GLB (sRGB hex converted to linear with c^2.2): Leaf #4F8A3C, LeafLight #7DAF55, Bark #8B7A70, Grass #5E9A3F.
details: Every pad and its branch hangs under its own pivot (sway_crown, sway_left, sway_right, sway_back, sway_swing) at the branch root. Each one sways 1.6 to 2.6 degrees on two axes with offset phases. The rope swing (swing_pivot, a child of sway_swing) swings +-22 degrees about its branch, twice per loop. Frames 1 to 120 at 24 fps, all sine-based, so the loop is seamless, and it exports as one 'Scene' clip.
Blender 5.2 (bpy), built from Python by the modeler, directed by the art director

Stepping-stone path leading to the door, iron hinges and a knob on the door, knots where the swing ropes meet the branch, small bushes and rocks around the roots, a back plate so the tree reads in the round, and the swing riding on its swaying branch (the hierarchy makes the two motions combine).

Only the lowest lid band carries wrap ridges; the other rims are smooth tubes.

steps: Midjourney drew end | long face | end, so views/ uses the long latch face as front (-Y), the left end as side (+X), and the long face mirrored as back (the sheet has no back view); prep_views.py also clips the cast shadows that touched the image edges and would have counted as object.

Every weft strand is a thin one-quad strip (1.5 cm tall, twice the rows of the first pass) whose depth goes over and under at each 5 cm stake, offset one stake per row and per face. The diving half of each cell is a ReedShade about 12% darker, and a mid-tone core behind the gaps keeps them as fine lines. The result reads as fine, even wicker rather than a checkerboard.
Lid on top, on a hinge

The lid is a separate pivot at the back edge of the rim. It has a fat rolled bottom band (3.1 cm) that overhangs the body, two stepped-in bands above it for a rounded shoulder, a domed woven top, a top roll and rope lashings at the hinge. A matching fat rolled band runs round the base.

The rope is laid-rope style: a 6-sided twisting profile with fat bulges and tight pinches. Handles are knotted through both ends. The latch is a loop tied to the lid front that drops over a wooden toggle, ending in a coiled knot and a tapering hanging tail.
0.70 m long body (0.87 m with handles), 0.33 m deep, 0.44 m tall, slight inward taper to the base; measured from the turnaround and tuned on IoU.
Honey wicker #B9763F for the reed (the render's mean comes out at sRGB 183,118,72), with rims a little darker and a 12% darker under-shade.
details: One 120-frame, 24 fps seamless clip ('Scene'). The lid rotates on a hinge at the back edge of the rim: it rests (1-18), lifts 72 degrees (18-44), holds open (44-76), closes (76-102) with a small landing bounce (102-112), and rests to 120. The latch loop hangs from a pivot at its knot on the lid front: it lags behind the lid, swings past plumb, settles hanging down while the lid is open, and drops back over the toggle peg as the lid closes.

steps: The sheet's views touch: the front hat overlaps the side view's basket in x, and the side hat touches the back hat. The floor contact shadow also counted as object, so the side view picked up a sliver of the front hat and the front mask ran the full panel width. prep_views.py rebuilds views/ from turnaround.png. It fits the backdrop gradient, paints out the floor shadow under the feet, makes clean cuts between views, and darkens cream areas inside the silhouette slightly so the harness keeps them. It also mirrors the side view, because the sheet draws her right side and the harness side camera looks at her left. All scores use `score r views`.

Built the signature shapes first: a big round head (0.47 m wide, about 30% of the height and about 45% with the hat crown) in a cream hood, a giant floppy straw hat (0.88 m brim, wider than the body) with a wavy brim that droops at the sides and back and curls up at the front, a carrot tucked in the rust band, a bell-shaped smock over a green skirt, stubby legs with pointed boots, and a staved wooden tub piled with vegetables and big leafy greens.

Dot eyes, rosy cheeks, a small open smile and a button nose; a ragged smock hem with ochre patches; a leather band across the chest and a pouch; a leather satchel of greens on her back; green sleeve cuffs; a tub with two hoops, a rim and a handle.

Rigid parts in a hierarchy: seller > body > neck (head, hood, face, hat > hat_brim_pivot > hat_brim, carrot), shoulders > arms, tub > bucket and veg, satchel, smock, skirt, strap. The legs stay planted on the ground. Each frame of the 120-frame loop is keyed from periodic functions, so frame 120 runs straight back into frame 1. It exports as one 'Scene' clip.

The hero and the sheet disagree in two places, and I followed the hero both times. The hero holds the tub on her right hip at the front with a satchel behind, while the sheet wears the tub as a backpack. The hero tucks the carrot on the left back of the crown, while the sheet tucks it on the right. Both choices cost IoU on the sheet views (see 'off').

The brim is generated as a wavy disc that curls up at the front to frame the face and flops at the sides and back, on its own pivot so it can flop in the idle.
